First to arrive were hundreds of Serb soldiers in what appeared to be a well-trained unit. They were dressed in camouflage uniforms and heavily armed. A group of 15 to 20 of them came to OP Papa and seized DutchBat equipment, including helmet, flak jackets, arms, and an APC. They also disconnected the OP's contact with the command. The Dutch soldiers, including Patelski, remained detained at OP Papa until 2100 hours that night. Three more groups of Serb soldiers arrived. Those in blue camouflage uniform identified themselves as being from a special police unit, while those in black overalls were part of an anti-terrorism unit. Patelski also saw another group of soldiers which he described as Rambo types, dressed in a mixture of civilian and military gear and well armed with grenades, AK-47s, and knives. From the roof of OP Papa, Patelski saw that those dressed in black uniforms had dogs and for several hours they cleared houses. First they threw in grenades, then they entered with the dogs and began shooting. This gave Patelski the impression that the Muslims who had been living in those houses were killed. The houses were then set on fire. General Mladic arrived at the OP during the afternoon and requested a meeting with Colonel Karremans. Karremans came to the OP and spoke to Mladic. After being detained at the OP all day, the DutchBat soldiers were transported to the Potocari compound that night. Once there, Patelski saw that the compound was flooded with refugees, at least a few thousand of them, mostly women and children. He found them to be terrified and in poor health. The next morning he saw about 15 buses parked outside the compound facing Bratunac. The evacuation of refugees began after 8.00 in the morning. Patelski helped with the evacuation of refugees by bringing refugees in groups to the edge of the compound. There the Serb soldiers dressed in camouflage uniforms and armed with AK-47 rifles separated the men from the women and children. Patelski took the rest of the refugees to the buses. Serb soldiers with guns stood near the buses, which terrified the people more. People looked at Patelski with death in their eyes, like they thought they would not survive the day. The men were taken to a grass field across the compound. Some Serb soldiers were beating them, even though the men were very weak and unarmed. At one point Patelski heard a shot in the field. He later saw the body of a dead man there. Later that day, more buses arrived and the men were taken in the direction of Bratunac. Five to six trips were required to take away at least a hundred men who'd been separated from the rest. Nearly all of the refugees were evacuated from the compound that day except some wounded people. A day after the evacuation, belongings abandoned by the refugees littered the Potocari compound. Mr. President, that concludes my summary and I only have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, were you stationed -- you were stationed at OP Papa; correct?

utterances.speaker: ROGER PATELSKI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I'd like to show you 65 ter 23517. This is a map. It will come on the screen but you also have a hard copy in front of you on the table.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And this map shows a road running south of Bratunac to Srebrenica, and we've pinpointed the Potocari compound and Yellow Bridge on the map. First of all, does this map look accurate to you? Are you familiar with this area?

utterances.speaker: ROGER PATELSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this map looks familiar to me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And the pinpoints of the UN Dutch compound and the Yellow Bridge, do those look to be in the right places?

utterances.speaker: ROGER PATELSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that's entirely correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: About how far north of Potocari was OP Papa located in terms of kilometres?

utterances.speaker: ROGER PATELSKI
utterances.text: That was approximately 1 kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I want to show you 65 ter 23518. It will come up on the screen. You also have a hard copy. This is essentially the exact same map but it's satellite footage. Now, you mentioned in your statement at paragraph 10 that before the attack in July you saw Serb military movement in the hills above Potocari. Are the elevations reflected on this map consistent with the hills that you saw around Potocari and OP Papa?

utterances.speaker: ROGER PATELSKI
utterances.text: Yes, they're the same hills, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And I wonder, Mr. President, if the witness can actually write on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: He may need some assistance for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to indicate on this map with a pen where you saw Serb military movement in the hills. And you can just write directly on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we ask him to mark the OP Papa first.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sergeant, if you could map -- mark OP Papa first.

utterances.speaker: ROGER PATELSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Looking at this aerial photograph that was taken from a great distance, it's a bit difficult for me to indicate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we zoom in further.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Once again. Just could you wait until being assisted by our usher. Do you think you can now mark it, Sergeant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You asked me whether I could indicate where the OP was at that time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It must have been approximately there. It was near Yellow Bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, can you also mark on this map the area where you saw Serb military movement in the hills?

utterances.speaker: ROGER PATELSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I'll indicate them generally. Somewhere in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And for the record, the smaller circle on the map is where the witness indicated OP Papa. The larger area is where he indicated Serb military movement.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Can you initial this and put the date, please, which is the 13th.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please consider the possibility of giving the precise dates when the Serb troops were there and how that relates to the borders of the protected area.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe that could be done on cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, but I was -- I was about to ask the question. The -- not time-frame, but you mean the area where you saw the Serb military exercise is -- was inside enclave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, at first I saw military movement by the Bosnian Serb army, and they were easily perceptible from our observation post. To the north-west of our observation post there were various hills and we were able to see in the top of the hills that they were building up reinforcements and fighting strength in the sense of mortars and other items. And further down between OP Papa and Yellow Bridge we identified two tanks. That was before the incursion into the enclave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. West, could you take up --

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. Patelski, I'll refer you to paragraph 10 in your amalgamated statement and ask you questions about that, where you noted that before the Serb offensive attack in July you saw Serb military movement in the hills above Potocari. So this larger circle that you've put on the screen is -- is that in reference to the military movement that you saw before the attack in July?

utterances.speaker: ROGER PATELSKI
utterances.text: Before the attack in July. Can I add something or draw a line to clarify?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Just a second. Shall we change the colour into blue now with the assistance of our usher. Could you wait a minute.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The reinforcement of troops that I perceived days before the enclave fell, and my co-workers did too, that was in the hills. I'm going to draw that on now. It was in this border area around -- that was for the Bosnian Serb army. It was -- they had good vision there and were easily able to look into the enclave from there. They had a good view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you initial -- put your initial and date of today at the end of the photo. 13th of January.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be next Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P4174, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note the time, Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask something? Perhaps it could be of assistance in saving time if the Defence does not have to take up time on matters that are not strictly necessary. May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Am I right in saying that in some other cases, especially in Popovic et al., the Prosecution abandoned qualifying the military operation in Srebrenica as illegitimate. If that is so, then I would not have to spend time proving that it was a legitimate act. But if I'm not correct in this assumption, I should know that now. A lot of time indeed could be saved if the military operation in Srebrenica is not considered as an unlawful act.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would like you to rephrase that submission in consultation with Robinson and after having a word have a discussion with the Prosecution, you can come up again to us. Mr. Patelski, your examination-in-chief was done by way of written statement and you'll be further asked by Mr. Karadzic in his cross-examination next week. Probably you are aware of this, but you are not supposed to discuss about your testimony with anybody else. Do you understand that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's entirely clear to me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll resume next Monday at 9.00. Please have a nice weekend, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 16th day of January, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.
